findings.anchor: .loop/plans/aim-to-apm.md (Could invalidate this plan; step 2 rules bullet)
findings.claim: python-testing changes from always-on to path-scoped in Claude, and the plan does not say so. aim's copy in .claude/rules/python-testing.md has no paths key, so Claude loads it in every session. At 1c3dd31 the upstream rules/python-testing.instructions.md carries applyTo "**/*.py". Spike 3 shows APM rewrites applyTo into a paths: list, so after the move the rule loads only once Claude touches a .py file. The other five skills-repo rules have no applyTo and stay always-on. OpenCode gets the same file through the step 6 copy but ignores paths:, so it keeps loading the rule always. The two harnesses then differ. The plan's risk text repeats the spike's 'no front matter, so Claude loads them always', which is wrong for this rule. A front-matter diff in the step 1 record does not count as the operator accepting a change to when the rule loads. Either get the operator's acceptance and state the new scope in the Outcome, or keep the rule always-on (for example, pin python-testing where it has no applyTo, if APM can install that file).

The Outcome needs both `just pre_commit` and `just check-install` to pass on a clean checkout. At HEAD they already conflict, and the plan adds more files to the area where they clash. The `end-of-file-fixer` hook in .pre-commit-config.yaml runs on .agents/, .opencode/ and opencode.json, because only .claude/ and .loop/ are excluded. APM and `kmctl plugin patch` write some files with no final newline. HEAD's .agents/skills/audit/evals/sample-findings.json ends in a newline (added by the fixer), but the copy APM installed, now staged in the index, does not. opencode.json shows the same split. So a frozen install on a clean checkout rewrites a committed file, and check-install fails before this ticket changes anything. The plan commits 12 more skill trees under .agents/skills/ and 7 rules under .opencode/rules/, and each one can hit the same clash. The plan neither scopes this nor lists it as a risk. It needs a step that settles which tool owns these paths, for example excluding APM-managed paths from end-of-file-fixer. That fix is a small edit to .pre-commit-config.yaml. Without it, the acceptance criteria cannot all be met. Spike to confirm the scope: on a clean worktree at HEAD, run `just check-install` and list the files it reports.
